pages.title: Usage
pages.description: Copy ignored files selected by .worktreeinclude between Git worktrees.
pages.body:
`waft` copies `.worktreeinclude`-selected ignored files between Git worktrees.
It is intended for local configuration, caches, and tool state that Git should
not track but that developers often need in more than one linked worktree.

## Quick start

```sh
# In a linked worktree, copy from the main worktree automatically.
waft

# Explicit source and destination.
waft copy --source /path/to/main --dest /path/to/linked

# See what would be copied without writing files.
waft copy --dry-run

# List eligible files.
waft list

# Inspect specific files.
waft info .env

# Validate ignore files.
waft validate
```

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `waft` / `waft copy` | Copy eligible files. This is the default command. |
| `waft list` | List eligible files without copying. |
| `waft info <PATH>...` | Show detailed status for specific files. |
| `waft validate` | Check ignore files for syntax errors. |

## Global options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--source <PATH>` | Source, usually the main worktree path. |
| `--dest <PATH>` | Destination, usually the linked worktree path. |
| `-C <PATH>` | Operate as if started in `PATH`. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Suppress non-error output. |
| `-v, --verbose` | Increase output verbosity. |

## Copy options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-n, --dry-run` | Show what would be done without copying. |
| `--overwrite` | Allow overwriting existing untracked destination files. |

## Typical flow

1. Add `.worktreeinclude` to the source repo.
2. Run `waft copy --dry-run`.
3. Inspect the plan.
4. Run `waft copy`.
5. Use `waft info <path>` when a file is missing or skipped.

pages.title: .worktreeinclude
pages.description: The include file format used by waft.
pages.body:
`.worktreeinclude` uses familiar `.gitignore` syntax to select ignored files
that `waft` should copy between worktrees.

```text
# Include environment files
.env
*.env.local

# Include all secret keys recursively
**/*.key

# But not test keys
!test.key
```

## Eligibility

A file is eligible for copying only when all of these are true:

1. It exists in the source worktree.
2. It is a regular file, not a symlink, directory, or special file.
3. It is selected by the active compatibility profile.
4. Git confirms it is ignored and untracked.
5. It is not dropped by the active exclusion set.

## Profile-dependent matching

By default, the `claude` profile only consults the root-level
`.worktreeinclude`.

Use `--compat-profile git` when you want nested `.worktreeinclude` files to
compose like nested `.gitignore` files. Use `--compat-profile wt` when you want
worktrunk-compatible all-ignored behavior.

## Validation

Run:

```sh
waft validate
```

Validation parses ignore files before copy execution. Copy planning remains
read-only until the command enters the execute phase.

pages.title: Safety
pages.description: The guarantees waft keeps while copying ignored worktree files.
pages.body:
`waft` is designed around a plan-then-execute pipeline. Discovery and
classification happen before any filesystem mutation.

## Guarantees

- **Tracked files are never overwritten.** Destination trackedness is checked
  before copy execution.
- **Symlink traversal is blocked.** `waft` refuses to follow symlinks in source
  files or write through symlinked destination parents.
- **Atomic writes.** Files are written to a temporary path and then renamed into
  place.
- **Dry runs are mutation-free.** `waft copy --dry-run` reads and reports only.

## Preview before writing

```sh
waft copy --dry-run
```

Use dry-run output to confirm which files would move and why.

## Overwrite behavior

Existing destination files are preserved by default. Use `--overwrite` only when
you intentionally want untracked destination files replaced.

```sh
waft copy --overwrite
```

`--overwrite` does not change the rule that tracked files are protected.

pages.title: Profiles
pages.description: Compatibility profiles for different worktree workflows.
pages.body:
`waft` ships with coordinated compatibility profiles. Each profile selects a
bundle of matcher and safety behavior.

| Profile | Missing `.worktreeinclude` | Matcher semantics | Symlinked rule files | Tool-state excludes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude` | nothing selected | `claude-2026-04` | follow | none |
| `git` | nothing selected | `git` | ignore | none |
| `wt` | every git-ignored untracked file selected | `wt-0.39` | follow | `tooling-v1` |

## `claude`

The default profile. It matches Claude Code's out-of-the-box behavior by using
the repository root `.worktreeinclude`.

```sh
waft copy --compat-profile claude
```

## `git`

Use this profile when you want Git-style per-directory exclude semantics, where
patterns are relative to the directory containing the file and deeper files can
override shallower files.

```sh
waft copy --compat-profile git
```

## `wt`

Use this profile for worktrunk parity. It starts from every git-ignored
untracked file and removes paths matched by literal-name negations.

```sh
waft copy --compat-profile wt
```

pages.title: Configuration
pages.body:
`waft` resolves profile and policy settings from multiple layers. Later layers
win for scalar values.

1. Built-in defaults.
2. User config: `~/.config/waft/config.toml`.
3. Project configs: each `.waft.toml` from repo root down to the current
   directory.
4. Environment variables using the `WAFT_*` prefix.
5. CLI flags.

Explicit knob settings always beat preset values from a higher-precedence
profile layer.

## Example `.waft.toml`

```toml
version = 1

[compat]
profile = "git"

[exclude]
extra = ["*.bak"]
```

## Per-knob CLI flags

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--compat-profile <claude\|git\|wt>` | Coordinated preset selection. |
| `--when-missing-worktreeinclude <blank\|all-ignored>` | Behavior when no `.worktreeinclude` exists. |
| `--worktreeinclude-semantics <claude-2026-04\|git\|wt-0.39>` | Matcher semantics version. |
| `--worktreeinclude-symlink-policy <follow\|ignore\|error>` | How to handle symlinked rule files. |
| `--builtin-exclude-set <none\|tooling-v1>` | Curated tool-state exclusion set. |
| `--extra-exclude <GLOB>` | Repeatable additional excludes. |
| `--replace-extra-excludes` | Drop inherited `extra-exclude` values. |
| `--config <PATH>` | Use this file instead of the default user config. |

pages.title: Architecture
pages.description: How waft plans and executes safe worktree file copies.
pages.body:
`waft` is built around a few invariant design decisions.

## Git is authoritative

`waft` does not reimplement Git's ignore logic for final ignored/tracked
decisions. Those checks go through the `GitBackend` trait.

- `GitGix` is the default in-process backend built on the `gix` crate.
- `GitCli` shells out to Git and is selected with `WAFT_GIT_BACKEND=cli`.

Backend parity tests keep both implementations aligned.

## `.worktreeinclude` matching is pluggable

`.worktreeinclude` files use `.gitignore` syntax, but selection is handled by
`worktreeinclude_engine`. Current engines are:

- `claude-2026-04`, the default root-rule-file behavior.
- `git`, Git-style per-directory exclude semantics.
- `wt-0.39`, worktrunk-compatible subtractive behavior.

## Commands plan before executing

All commands follow a read-only planning pipeline before writes are possible.

1. Parse CLI arguments.
2. Resolve layered policy.
3. Resolve source and destination worktree context.
4. Validate ignore files.
5. Select candidate files.
6. Apply policy filters.
7. Confirm ignored status through Git.
8. Build a copy plan.
9. Execute only for `copy` without `--dry-run`.

`list`, `info`, and `validate` never enter the execute phase.

## Testing strategy

The test suite combines unit tests, integration tests against real Git repos,
profile coverage tests, backend parity tests, and differential/property tests
against a Git oracle for `git` semantics.
